The tie rule only orders simultaneous completions. For Malenia every completion counts (counts B_j += 1) until the harmonic exit, so ties can change which worker's count is incremented at the exit instant. This affects neither the exit time nor the validity of the exit counts (any order of simultaneous events is a legitimate realization of 'wait for the next worker'), and Exec64 quantifies the counts existentially from the actual run.

completion V s = some (sInf {t | s <= t and V s + 1 <= V t}) if that set is nonempty, else none: the first time the work since s reaches 1. The elaborated value is identical to the declaration I accepted in the Theorem 5.3 run.

earliest c l = foldr (earliestStep c) none l, where earliestStep skips undefined times and keeps the smaller time, with ties going to the lowest index. It returns a minimal defined finish time, or none if no worker ever finishes. The elaborated value is identical to the declaration I accepted in the Theorem 5.3 run.
earliestStep c i r: if c i is none then r; otherwise (i, a) when r is none or a <= r's time, else r. The elaborated value is identical to the declaration I accepted in the Theorem 5.3 run.

notes: For Malenia, the tie rule can decide which worker's count is incremented at the exit instant when completions coincide. Exec64's counts are taken from the actual run, and any order of simultaneous completions is a valid realization of Method 4, so this is harmless. At the timing64 review, round_step_h must not assume a specific tie order beyond what earliest provides.
